goal: Coordinate Feishu organization identity, company permission truth, purpose-bound OAuth, token lifecycle, and task return across web, Feishu H5, company homepage, and desktop entrypoints.

target_architecture.sync_strategy: database-change trigger plus daily full reconciliation
target_architecture.token_boundary: employee cookie, desktop session, and cloud-document grant are isolated
target_architecture.task_return: cloud-document reauthorization resumes the original draft

acceptance_criteria.description: The authorization snapshot projects stable Feishu identity mappings and subject-bound company permission assignments without deriving business permissions from departments or organization roles.
Vercel distinguishes missing, invalid, stale, and unavailable snapshot states from employee identity denial and exposes a non-PII health result.

Company administration authorization is finally decided by enabled dc_admin permission records with global scope and cannot be granted by department, relation_type, legacy role, or a hardcoded open ID.
OAuth transactions use signed short-lived state, a purpose, one-time nonce consumption, an allowlisted return target, and purpose-specific session or token output.
Cloud-document authorization uses a one-time handoff and rotatable opaque grant, refreshes or reauthorizes after expiry, and returns to the original draft instead of entering employee desktop login.
Identity or permission database changes trigger synchronization while a daily reconciliation task repairs missed events, and the task is installable, observable, and removable.
Disabled or departed employees cannot obtain a new web session, desktop refresh, or cloud-document refresh even when an old permission assignment or token exists.
